messages:
hema: Heads up — we keep getting inconsistent 429 headers from hosted endpoints when using the Python SDK. Names and formats vary (Retry-After as seconds, HTTP-date, x-rl-reset-in, x-ratelimit-reset as epoch or delta). Breaking our simple backoff.

ben: Can you paste examples?

hema: Sure, real logs: 
```
Retry-After: 30
retry-after: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT
x-ratelimit-reset: 1720000000
x-rl-reset-in: 20
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Limit: 100/3600
```

hema: Also seeing vendor keys like `x-rl-ttl` and some services fold limit as `100/3600` which we should parse.

ben: Proposal: expose two helpers in the SDK: `parse_retry_after(v: Optional[str]) -> Optional[float]` (seconds until retry) and `parse_ratelimit_headers(headers: Mapping[str,str]) -> RateLimitInfo`. RateLimitInfo should be a frozen dataclass with keys: `limit`, `remaining`, `reset_at`(epoch), `reset_in`, and `raw` map. Keep types simple so mypy users are happy.

mira: We need an async client-side limiter too. Current internal script has a sync token-bucket. Suggest `redwood.utils.throttling.AsyncTokenBucket` with `async with limiter.acquire(tokens=1):` and `try_acquire()` returning bool. Make it cancellation-friendly and efficient (no busy loop).

ben: Edge cases: for `x-ratelimit-reset` numeric values > 1e11 should be considered epoch; small numbers are seconds-until-reset. Cap parsed values to a sane max (7 days). Treat negative `Retry-After` as 0.

hema: For SDK UX: add `ClientConfig.auto_retry=True` and a strategy option "respect-retry-after" which prefers Retry-After header when present, falling back to expo+jitter. Document that streaming endpoints are excluded from auto-retry.

tool-bot: Created issue #5502: "py-sdk: ratelimit header normalization + helpers + async token-bucket" assigned to @devex-team.

mira: I'll prototype the AsyncTokenBucket and an example `examples/async_ratelimit_demo.py`. ben: I'll own the parsing helpers + tests. hema: I'll draft the RFC for dataclass shape and signatures.

hema: Also request: include the raw header dict on RateLimitInfo so consumers can log vendor-specific keys for debugging.

ben: Agreed. Small PRs first: parsing helpers -> tests -> async limiter -> example.

hema: Thanks everyone — landing RFC today.
